summary: ICT toolkit: inversion FVGs, CISD lines, HTF gaps, weekly, daily and session highs and lows, session boxes and SMT against a paired symbol.
overview: This community script gathers ICT reference points in one overlay. It draws inversion fair value gaps after liquidity sweeps, CISD lines, and the nearest unmitigated higher-timeframe gap on each side. It marks previous week and day highs and lows, Asia and London highs and lows, the all-time high, and the 8:30 AM New York open.
It also shades Asia, London, NY AM and NY PM sessions, and draws SMT divergence lines between the chart and a correlated symbol.
how: After a sweep, the most recent qualifying FVG that price closes through is drawn as an inversion box; pending gaps can be shown first and are removed if they never invert. The open of the delivering leg is tracked, and a close back through it prints a CISD line. A CISD whose implied stop is broken is removed.
Higher-timeframe gaps come from two timeframes chosen from the chart interval. Levels close to each other (within 8 ticks by default) share one label.
SMT pairs are automatic for NQ-ES, MNQ-MES, YM-ES, MYM-MES, GC-SI and MGC-SIL, or manual. A sensitivity setting sets swing size for the three-point pattern, and an optional mode adds gap divergence.
use: Use the level labels to see where key highs and lows sit before the session opens.
Some traders watch inversion FVGs and CISDs that form after a sweep of a marked level.
Use session boxes to see which session made the high or low of the day.
Watch SMT lines when the chart and its paired market disagree at a swing.
notes: Session times are New York time; session labels show on 15-minute and lower charts.
SMT needs data for the correlated symbol and is made for the futures and metal pairs listed.
The script has no alert conditions.
